drills.q: A request fails with PERMISSION_DENIED naming an IAM deny policy. The caller has roles/owner. What happened and what are the options?
drills.a: Deny policies outrank every allow including Owner. Options: use the exceptionPrincipals path (break-glass principal carved out of the rule), or have a deny-admin modify the rule. There is no allow that overrides it.

drills.q: Your CI needs to deploy Cloud Run services as a dedicated SA. Which two grants does the pipeline identity need, and where?
drills.a: roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on the deploy SA (if federated) so it can impersonate, plus roles/iam.serviceAccountUser (actAs) on the runtime SA so deployments can attach it; deployment roles bound to the deploy or runtime SA in the target project.

drills.q: Design the WIF setup for one GitHub org with 40 repos where only repo 'api' may touch production.
drills.a: Pool + OIDC provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com with attribute condition repository_owner_id == <your-org-id>; bind workloadIdentityUser to principalSet filtered on attribute.repository/my-org/api impersonating the prod-deploy SA. Two gates: condition at provider, selector at binding.

drills.q: Pods get 403s after you annotated the KSA correctly. Give three causes ranked by likelihood.
drills.a: 1) Workload Identity not enabled on cluster or node pool (no metadata config). 2) workloadIdentityUser bound to the wrong principal string (project number vs id, namespace/name typo). 3) Binding granted to namespace-wide principalSet but GSA itself lacks resource roles â€” check both hops.

drills.q: Security wants 'nobody can ever create service account keys' enforced. Name the two complementary controls and their gap.
drills.a: Org policy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation (blocks configuration path, supports dry-run first) plus IAM deny policy on iam.googleapis.com/serviceAccountKeys.create as request-time backstop with break-glass exception. Gap: deny coverage is permission-subset â€” verify; also enforce key upload ban.

drills.q: A contractor needs viewer on staging only, expiring in 30 days. Implement without human babysitting.
drills.a: Binding with CEL condition: resource-tag match env=staging AND request.time < timestamp('2026-09-22T00:00:00Z'). Note tokens minted before expiry stay valid until their own expiry; pair with short-lived access (impersonation) if revocation matters.

drills.q: Troubleshooter says ALLOW but the API call still fails. List four non-IAM layers to check.
drills.a: VPC Service Controls perimeter denial, org-policy enforcement blocking the write, CMEK key permissions missing for the service agent, quota/limits errors. Read the exact error string â€” each layer phrases denial differently.

drills.q: 500 projects still run workloads as the Editor-granted default compute SA. Sequence the migration.
drills.a: 1) Audit actual API usage per default SA from audit logs. 2) Create per-workload SAs with observed-minimal predefined roles. 3) Roll service-by-service behind explicit SA config. 4) Enforce via org policy/deny that default SAs get no new editor grants. Measure before removing.

drills.q: Why is granting TokenCreator broadly worse than serviceAccountUser?
drills.a: actAs still requires launching/attaching a resource (auditable creation event); TokenCreator mints ~1h tokens via API directly â€” silent full impersonation, no resource trail beyond the mint call itself. Scope TokenCreator to specific signing/minting workloads only.

drills.q: Multi-customer SaaS: which GCP primitive gives the hardest tenant boundary and why?
drills.a: Project-per-tenant(-tier): IAM inheritance, quotas, networking defaults all stop at project edges â€” the oldest hard boundary. Layer conditions/PAB/VPC-SC as refinement; folder+tags+conditions alone leaves softer edges.

drills.q: A workload identity pool provider's attribute condition was loosened during a migration and nobody noticed for three weeks. What's the blast radius and how do you detect this class of incident?
drills.a: Blast radius is every external caller the IdP itself considers valid for that provider -- e.g. any repo in the entire GitHub org, not just the intended one -- able to impersonate whichever service account the pool's bindings allow, for the whole exposure window. Detect via Cloud Audit Logs alerts on pool/provider config changes, plus runtime monitoring of STS token-exchange logs for unexpected source attribute values (e.g. a spike in distinct repository claims against a pool meant to serve one repo).
